entries.target: wine:Cesarini Sforza Rosé Brut Trento NV
entries.value: The Cesarini Sforza Rosé Brut is a Trento DOC sparkling rosé from Trento, in the Italian Alps: mostly Chardonnay, with a little Pinot Noir for its colour. It is made the Champagne way, its second fermentation in the bottle followed by about three years on its lees. It is dry and fresh: small red berries, a bright mountain acidity and a soft mousse. Its cold fizz suits fried snacks and hot sauce at the Roost Bar. We pour it at 43 to 46°F in a flute or tulip, in two stages. The house dates from 1974, and its eagle emblem is the coat of arms of Trento.

entries.value: The Jansz Premier Cuvée Brut 2022 is sparkling wine from Pipers River in Tasmania, the cool island south of mainland Australia: Chardonnay and Pinot Noir. It is made by the traditional method, with its second fermentation in the bottle, and breezes off the Bass Strait keep the ripening slow and the acidity high. It tastes crisp and clean, of citrus and green apple with a hint of brioche, a salty tang and fine bubbles. That tang suits salt and spice at the Roost Bar. We pour it at 43 to 46°F in a flute or tulip. Jansz began in 1986 as a venture with the Champagne house Louis Roederer.

entries.target: wine:Chapel Down Rosé Brut Kent NV
entries.value: The Chapel Down Rosé Brut is English sparkling rosé from Kent, led by Chardonnay and Pinot Noir with a little Meunier. It is made by the traditional method, with about eighteen months on its lees in the bottle. Dry and light, it tastes of strawberry and red currant, with bright English acidity and fine bubbles. It is our value bottle for the Steak Tartare Cannoli, its red fruit meeting the raw beef while the bubbles lift the crème fraîche. We pour it at 43 to 46°F in a flute or tulip, in two stages. Its home vineyard at Tenterden was first planted in 1977.

entries.value: Ridgeview Bloomsbury Brut is English sparkling wine from Ditchling, in Sussex, on the chalk of the South Downs: mostly Chardonnay, with Pinot Noir and Meunier. It is made by the traditional method, with a second fermentation in the bottle. It tastes of lemon zest, green apple and toasted brioche, with crisp acidity and a fine mousse. It is our value bottle for the Eggs Hussarde, that acidity cutting the hollandaise and the yolk. We pour it at 43 to 46°F in a tulip or white-wine glass. The estate was founded in the mid 1990s to make only sparkling wine, and its wines carry the names of London districts.

entries.value: The Domaine Huet Pétillant 2019 is a lightly sparkling Vouvray, all Chenin Blanc, from the Loire near Tours. It is made by the traditional method but to about half the usual pressure, then rests at least three years on its lees, so the fizz is soft and creamy. It tastes of quince, apple and honeysuckle, held up by Chenin's high, bright acidity. That acidity stands up to vinegar and frying at the Roost Bar. We pour it at 43 to 46°F in a tulip or white-wine glass, easing the cork out gently. Victor and Anna-Constance Huet bought their first Vouvray vineyard, Le Haut-Lieu, in 1928.

entries.value: The Ferrari Rosé Brut is a Trento DOC sparkling rosé from the Italian Alps, about 60 percent Pinot Noir and 40 percent Chardonnay, picked by hand. It is made by the traditional method and rests at least twenty months on its lees. It is dry, with real body for a pink sparkler: wild strawberry, raspberry, fresh mountain acidity and a creamy mousse. That body suits fried pastry and a creamy rémoulade. We pour it at 43 to 46°F in a flute or tulip, in two stages. Giulio Ferrari founded the house in Trento in 1902, after learning the Champagne method in Épernay; it is no relation to the cars.

entries.value: JM Sélèque Solessence is a grower Champagne from Pierry, just south of Épernay: about half Chardonnay, the rest Meunier and a little Pinot Noir, from the family's vines in seven villages. Part is fermented in oak, and half the blend comes from a perpetual reserve begun in 2004. Extra Brut, so very dry, it tastes of white flowers, ripe citrus and almond paste, chalky and precise. That dryness stands up to vinegar, frying and raw oysters. We pour it at 45 to 48°F in a tulip or white-wine glass, a touch warmer than the house bubbles. The family planted its first vines near Pierry in 1965.

entries.value: The Billecart-Salmon Réserve Brut is the family house's Brut, from Mareuil-sur-Aÿ in the Vallée de la Marne: Meunier, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, blended with reserve wines from older harvests. It is fresh and delicate rather than heavy, with pear, citrus, a light brioche and a clean finish. It is our classic bottle for the Steak Tartare with Rye, its acidity cutting the yolk and the raw beef. We pour it at 43 to 46°F in a tulip or white-wine glass, turning the bottle as we ease the cork. The house was founded in 1818 on the marriage of Nicolas François Billecart and Elisabeth Salmon.
